prerequisites: PHYSICS II: Electrical physics; knowledge regarding DC and AC current

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The capacity to analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant analytical, computational and experimental methods already established and correctly interpret the results of such analyzes.

Engineering analysis: The capacity to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; choose and apply appropriate analytical, computational and experimental methods already established; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems of their specialty, that comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.

Research and innovation: Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other sources of information, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project and research and their limitations in the field of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the field of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Elaboration of judgments: Capacity to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Capacity to communicate effectively information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Capacity to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Continuous training: Capacity to recognize the need for continuous self-training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Continuous training: Capacity to keep up to date with new developments in science and technology.
Define the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each of them, and making correct use of language, in writing.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Industrial Automation: advantages, disadvantages...
Types of Industrial Control: ON-OFF, PID
teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memoranda, audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs, individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Professor's presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Performing exercises individually and in teams
Resolution and performance of exercises, problems and practical work individually and in teams
Practical work in workshops and/or laboratories, individually or in teams

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, presentation and technical defense
Written and oral individual tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on the realization of exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For most learning outcomes (ENAxxx, RG304, RG302, RG301), assessment is 100% based on technical capacity, project/PBL involvement, work performed, results, documentation, and technical defense, with continuous assessment and project feedback. For RGM305, evaluation is 49.2% written/oral tests, 32.8% reports on exercises/practices, and 18% technical capacity/project work. For RGM308, it's 20% written/oral tests, 40% reports, and 40% technical capacity/project work; practical work cannot be recovered as it involves continuous faculty interaction, and the theoretical Grafcet value is 25% of the first control point plus 75% of the recovery. For RGM306, it's 36% written/oral tests, 44% reports, and 20% technical capacity/project work; sensor theory grade is 0.25 * 1st Control Point + 0.75 * recovery control point. For RGM309, it's 50% reports and 50% technical capacity/project work, based on continuous assessment and feedback from project and group work, requiring periodic meetings with experts. For RGM307, it's 64% written/oral tests, 16% reports, and 20% technical capacity/project work. Recovery mechanisms generally mirror the initial assessment methods for tests and technical/project work.
